title: World Cup Day 1: Mexico beat South Africa 2-0; South Korea beat Czechia 2-1
excerpt: Group stage action from Mexico City, Guadalajara on June 11 — 2 matches, no shortage of drama.
body:
Day 1 of the 2026 FIFA World Cup delivered 2 matches and 5 goals on Thursday, June 11. The tournament, spread across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, continued its group stage with action that will resonate in standings tables and living rooms alike — not least in the Indian-American households tuning in from cities that are, for once, hosting the spectacle rather than streaming it from half a world away.

Here is everything you need to know.

Mexico 2-0 South Africa

Group A · Mexico City Stadium, Mexico City

!World Cup — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

Mexico put in a controlled, professional performance to dispatch South Africa 2-0 at Mexico City Stadium. It was the kind of win that doesn't make highlight reels but earns respect in tournament football — composed at the back, incisive going forward, and ruthless when it mattered.

For South Africa, the two-goal deficit is not insurmountable, but their remaining Group A fixtures now carry the weight of must-win encounters.

"It was the kind of win that doesn't make highlight reels but earns respect in tournament football — composed at the back, incisive going forward, and ruthless when it mattered."

South Korea 2-1 Czechia

Group A · Estadio Guadalajara, Guadalajara

!Mexico City Stadium — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

In a tightly contested Group A opener, South Korea edged Czechia 2-1 in a match that swung on fine margins. The game had the tension of a knockout tie rather than a group stage opener, with both sides pressing hard and leaving little space in midfield.

Czechia will feel they deserved more, but tournament football is unforgiving. The single goal separating the teams belies how close Czechia came to snatching a point. They remain very much alive in Group A.

What It Means for the Standings

!Mexico City — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

In Group A, Mexico move to 3 points and put themselves in a strong position; South Korea move to 3 points and put themselves in a strong position; South Africa sit on zero points and will need results in their remaining fixtures; Czechia sit on zero points and will need results in their remaining fixtures.

With 48 teams and a format that sends the top two from each group — plus the eight best third-placed sides — into the round of 32, the margins are tighter than they appear. Goal difference could prove decisive.

What's Next

Day 2 (Friday, June 12) brings 2 more group stage matches:

  • Canada vs Bosnia & Herzegovina — Group B at BMO Field, Toronto
  • USA vs Paraguay — Group D at SoFi Stadium, Los Angeles
